observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale: a pale cream segmented grub with dark brown saddle patches on its back, each patch studded with small amber eyes, and rows of pink conical prolegs with dark claw tips. In every facing the head end is clamped by a ribbed pink collar onto a knot of olive-brown twisting roots that carry large veined eyeballs with green irises. South: the head and root knot toward the viewer, the body going back and up. East: a long, low side profile with the root knot at the right end rising into a vertical root stalk. North: the tail end toward the viewer, body going back, root knot and eyes at the far top.
observed.south.png: Front three-quarter view from above. The root mass with four big eyeballs is in the foreground. A thick root goes into the grub's round, ribbed pink mouth collar. Behind it the foreshortened back shows four dark saddles with clusters of small eyes, and paired conical legs on both sides. Clean transparent background.
observed.east.png: Side profile of the grub lying flat and straight, about 8 segments, with clawed conical prolegs underneath touching a ground line. A pink, ringed, funnel-like mouth collar at the right end fits over a root knot. Roots spread low under the head, and one root stalk climbs upward carrying three or four eyeballs. No curl. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view from above: the tail end is nearest, ending in a fan of clawed prolegs. The back saddles with small eyes run away from the viewer to the head, where the root knot with three large eyeballs and wavy tendrils sticks up past the far end. No mouth or face is visible. The only eyes are the dorsal eye-spots and the tree-root eyeballs. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: Next to the vanilla human at max zoom the grub is a small streak about a third of a cell long, with a tiny root tuft. At normal play (32 px/cell) it is a faint grey few-pixel smudge, barely visible beside the human and smaller than the rat silhouette.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: The head and mouth collar on the root face the camera. The body recedes behind them.

NORTH_REAR.seen: The tail end and its fan of prolegs face the camera. There is no mouth or face. The eyes visible are dorsal eye-spots that appear on every facing, plus the tree-root eyeballs at the far end. None of them is a face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: South and north are steep elevated views of a low, flat body, which shows a lot of back but is still foreshortened toward the camera. North is close to overhead: the body hardly foreshortens.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 60% spread comes from the pose. East is a horizontal profile of a long, low body, so it is short. North is tall because the root tendrils stick up past the head. Body width is about the same (~230 px) in south and north on the shared panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same cream body, dark eye-saddles, pink prolegs and pink mouth collar on the root knot appear on all three. The roots stay at the head end and turn with the body: foreground in south, right end in east, far end in north.

SIGNATURE.seen: A grub latched by its socket mouth onto eye-bearing ocular-tree roots, low to the ground and wingless. It reads clearly in south and east.

ALIEN.seen: The silhouette is caterpillar-like, but the eye-studded saddles, socket-collar mouth and eyeball roots keep a stranger from calling it an Earth larva at a glance.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 present: a round, ribbed socket collar is the head's dominant feature, with no mandibles. 2 present: the collar is clamped onto a root in south and east, feeding, not in soil. 3 present: the root mass carries large veined eyeballs. 4 present: no wings, and east shows the body straight and pressed low; it is not curled into a C, though it lies on the ground rather than along the root.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic in texture: ribbed flesh, veined eyeballs, bark-like roots. Not cel-shaded and not cute. The eyeballs are glossy, but they belong to the tree, not to a face.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art. Nothing like it exists in vanilla or a known mod.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on all three facings, with no ground patch or shadow. The root knot is part of the subject, as departure 3 requires, not a baked backdrop.

SCALE.seen: drawSize 0.32 makes it a small grub, about a third of a cell, beside the human. That fits 'grub', but it is very small.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it is a faint grey streak a few pixels long. The root knot and eye-saddles cannot be told apart from the ground.

edits.change: In the east profile the grub's whole underside lies flat along a thick horizontal root that runs beneath its head, abdomen and tail; the round socket mouth is clamped onto the root at the head end, and the body is pressed low and straight along the root's length.
One continuous feeding root extends under the full length of the grub, ending in the ocular tree's root mass at the tail side, so the body rests on the root from mouth to tail tip.

The north view is a rear view seen from behind: a smooth, segmented, pale dorsal back with soft ridged segment lines and a tapered tail end, the head tucked away at the far end. The only eyes in the image are the eye-like structures growing on the tree roots around it.

mouth socket latched onto a root in the act of feeding, not burrowing in soil

request.prompt: A single sparkleech grub, a pale, soft, segmented, wingless larva shown in the act of feeding at the roots of an ocular tree, painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background. Body plan: a long, plump, ridged segmented body with a tapered tail, pressed low and straight along the ground, not curled into a C. The head ends in a round, socket-like mouth opening as its dominant feature, a circular sucking ring rather than a beetle larva's chewing jaws. The grub's whole underside lies flat along a thick horizontal root that runs beneath its head, abdomen and tail; the socket mouth is clamped onto that root at the head end, feeding. The root is continuous under the full length of the body and leads into the ocular tree's root mass at the tail side, where gnarled roots bear visible eye-like structures (round lidded eyes with pupils set into the wood). The grub's own body is smooth and eyeless: a pale segmented back with soft ridged segment lines. Facing views: east and west are side profiles with the body lying along the root and the mouth at the head end; south is a front view, seen from the front with the round socket mouth toward the viewer, clamped on the root; north is a rear view, seen from behind, showing the segmented back and tapered tail with the head hidden, the only eyes in the image belonging to the tree roots. Small creature, reads clearly at tiny size.
